text:
A: Hello! Oh, it's you, the girl with the beautiful smile! I'm Danuta.
B: Aw, hiya! I'm Lauren. Oh, I've been wanting to talk to you, I saw your photo and I thought, she looks lovely, she'd make you a brew.
A: Of course I make you a brew! And cake. Have you had your tea yet, love?
B: Not yet, it'll be a cheese cob, honestly, me boyfriend's on shifts so I don't bother. Where are you, duck?
A: Preston. But I'm from Poland, near Rzeszów. You?
B: Derby. Chaddesden. What do you do?
A: I clean at the hospital, on the wards. Eleven years same two wards. I love the patients, the old ladies, they tell me all their stories. But my knees, oh, after an early shift, finished.
B: Oh, that's me old job sort of! Not the cleaning, I mean the older ladies. I was a fitness instructor and I loved the oldies, they were my favourites. I used to do chair classes and that, for people with dodgy knees.
A: Chair classes! This exists? Maybe I need this.
B: Honestly, you'd love it, it's all sat down, bit of music, arms going, nobody judges. I want to set up my own one day, in church halls round Derby. Dance for women and older ladies.
A: Oh, this is a beautiful idea. In my church, in Preston, the ladies would come, I know. They love music. I sing in the choir sometimes.
B: Do you? Oh, I love that. I was a dancer, I did a bit of a dance degree, but I sort of dropped out. Still annoys me, to be honest.
A: You were young. When you are young you make decisions, then you go another way. Is not the end.
B: Yeah. I know. I lost the job five months ago, they cut the timetable, so I'm signing on, and money's, you know... Sorry, I don't know why I'm telling you all this.
A: No, no, tell me. Is hard. When we came here, my husband and me, we had nothing, I worked in a chicken factory. Now look, I'm on the ward, everybody knows my name. You will find something, I'm sure. You have a face people like.
B: Oh, stop it, you'll set me off. Thank you, though. Do you watch Strictly? Tell me you watch Strictly.
A: Every Saturday! My husband falls asleep, I watch alone and I shout at the judges.
B: Same! I shout at the telly at the Rams and at Strictly, me dad says I'm a nightmare.
A: Ha! Who you like this year?
B: Oh, I'm rubbish with names, I just like the big group numbers, all the choreography. Me and me mum go to musicals at Derby Theatre when we can afford it.
A: My granddaughter, she dances now, five years old, in a little pink skirt. Too beautiful.
B: Aw, bless her. You need to get her in a class early, they love it at that age.
A: Yes! And you come to Preston and teach the grandmas. Then my knees get better too.
B: Deal. I'll need loads of tea and cake, mind.
A: This is easy. I have sixty pierogi in the freezer, so you never go—
